title: Weighted Fourier sum bound for functions far from linear
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_p^n \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ be normalized and $\varepsilon$-far from linear: that is, $f(0) = 0$, the parameter satisfies $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear $g : \mathbb{Z}_p^n \to \mathbb{Z}_p$. Write $\widetilde{f}(x) = \omega_p^{f(x)}$ for the lift of $f$ to the $p$-th roots of unity, and $\hat{\widetilde{f}}(s)$ for its Fourier coefficient at frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n$. Then
\[
  \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_p^n}
    \bigl|\hat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr|^2 \,
    \operatorname{Re}\bigl[\hat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
  1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\varepsilon .
\]
hypotheses_covered: dist(f,g) ≥ ε for every linear g
